summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on fraud/security, regulation.

articles.title: FTC aims to better fight scams
articles.description: To combat rising fraud, the Federal Trade Commission may update a rule that could make technology companies more liable when fraud occurs.

articles.title: Merchants sue feds over Illinois card fee law
articles.description: Trade groups filed lawsuits against bank and credit union regulators over a preemption of a state law that bans swipe fees for taxes and tips.

articles.title: Fiserv preps debit network sale
articles.description: The processing giant is shifting customers to one of its debit networks in anticipation of selling or shuttering a second one, the company’s CEO said Tuesday.

articles.title: Western Union, Intermex clash
articles.description: The money transfer services company dropped its acquisition of the smaller rival after California regulators weighed in, but now a fight over the deal has ensued.

articles.title: Block’s Cash App weaves payment tech into bandanas
articles.description: The peer-to-peer payment provider will soon begin selling its digital tags attached to bandanas.

articles.title: States keep targeting card fee relief
articles.description: Despite legal challenges to the Illinois Interchange Fee Prohibition Act, more than 30 interchange relief bills have been introduced in statehouses this year.

articles.title: Block to provide data to FTC
articles.description: The company said it will turn over documents the Federal Trade Commission sought in January in response to a probe of complaints about Square.

articles.title: Global Payments faces industry pricing pressure
articles.description: While analysts point to an increasingly competitive environment for the processor, the company is still trying to raise prices.
